items.discussion: layout-46 (Order 46); sweeps/order46/REPORT-layout-46.md; repro sweeps/order46/layout-46/finds/fenced_twin (node entry; `vilan check .`); blocks F28's first half for `std::web::router`
items.title: a file declaring `[platform("browser")] mod self;` that IMPORTS a platform-twin module (`std::web::ui`) is refused in a node build even when nothing reaches it from the entry: the import binds the PROCESS twin, and the fence walk reports that twin's functions ("`view` requires the `process` layer of `std` and cannot run on `browser` … reachable from `card`, which its declaration fences")
items.body: Repro: a node entry that imports `pkg::widget::card`, where `widget.vl` is `[platform("browser")] mod self;` + `import std::web::ui::{ View, view };` + `export fun card(): View { view("div") }`. `vilan check` on next: one error inside std's process `ui.vl`. One program has one platform, so a twin import resolves to the build platform's side, and the fence walk then checks a browser-fenced body against the OTHER twin. With a layer the same module (std's `router`, which imports `ui`) was loaded for typing and never fence-walked, so the layer gave zero errors; fenced it gives six on a bare `import std::web::router::location_url;` — the first of the two reasons layout-46 stopped F28. Rec: the fence walk skips a fenced body whose declaration this build's platform does not admit (it is dead in this build by its own declaration, and reachability from the entry already reports a real call into it), or reports only from entry-reachable fenced bodies. Pin: `module_resolution::f28_an_off_platform_call_into_a_single_platform_module_is_one_error_at_the_call` over a fenced tree.

items.title: importing `std::web::document` in a browser build fails INSIDE std — "cannot find 'escape_attribute' in the imported path" (and `escape_text`): `document.vl` imports them from `pkg::web::ui`, and only the PROCESS twin declares them
items.body: Pre-existing (the same on next before A154, as `std::document`, and under F28's fence). `import std::web::document::check_shell; fun main() {}` with `target = "browser"` reports four resolution errors attributed to std's `document.vl` instead of nothing (the import is elidable) or one platform refusal at a reaching call. Rec: `document.vl` takes the two escapers from a base module (they are pure string functions), or the twin parity gate lists them as process-only and the import moves behind the process layer's own surface. Pin: a browser build importing `std::web::document` without reaching it checks clean.

items.title: `infer_platform` reads browser evidence only off std's LAYER directories: a module that declares `[platform("browser")] mod self;` (std's, after F28, or a dependency library's) is not evidence, so a file importing only it is analysed under the default node platform
items.body: The second reason layout-46 stopped F28: with std's four browser modules fenced in the base root, a file importing only `std::web::dom` analysed as `node` ("no project sets its platform and nothing in it is browser-only") where the layer gave `browser` ("it imports `std::web::dom`, which only the browser layer serves"). Rec: a module whose file leads with a browser-only declaration is browser evidence exactly as a browser-layer-only module is (read through the parse cache, as `declares` already does). Pin: `module_resolution::f28_a_file_importing_only_a_single_platform_module_is_analyzed_as_before` over a fenced tree.

items.title: the auto-import completion table walks a package's TOP-LEVEL modules only: a name declared in a nested module (A65's `pkg::lib::ui::widget`) is never offered for auto-import
items.body: layout-46 made the walk descend std's namespaces (std's modules moved under `std::web::` and friends, and the table would otherwise have lost every one) and deliberately left `pkg`'s nested modules out, to change nothing else. The add-import QUICK FIX has the same top-level limit for `pkg` (`import_candidates` lists nested modules for std only). Rec: walk `pkg` the same way. Pins: a nested pkg module's name offered once, at its full path.

items.title: the A154 moved-path fix on `std::web::{ Signal, dom::create_element }` rewrites `web` to `web::prelude`, which breaks the sibling `dom::create_element` in the same brace list
items.body: The refusal for the old web-prelude path anchors at `web` (the segment that names it), and the fix replaces that segment; a brace list under `web` that mixes a prelude name with a real child module is the one shape where that edit is wrong for the siblings. Rec: in that shape, move the prelude names into their own `prelude::{ .. }` branch instead (`std::web::{ prelude::Signal, dom::create_element }`), or offer no edit. Rare: the old path never had children.

items.kind: bug (module resolution; prelude) — FIXED by layout-46
items.title: a `prelude` that names a module in a module DIRECTORY (`pkg::preludes::app`, and std's own `std::web::prelude` after A154) was never loaded — the seed took exactly two segments — nor resolved — `prelude_module_scope` did not descend a module's children — so the package silently got no ambient names
items.body: Fixed with A154 (the web prelude moved to `std::web::prelude`, which is how it showed: every web example lost `view`/`Signal`). Pinned by every web-prelude test on the tree.

items.title: `vilan fmt` declined every file that leads with `[platform(..)] mod self;` and carries `export *;`: E181's marker slot counted from the top of the file and put `export *;` above `mod self;`

`check_library_contract` walked a root's TOP-LEVEL modules only, so a module nested in a layer (A65) was never checked — after A154 that was every layered std module, and `vilan check` on std still said "platform contract OK"
